correctness.rationale: Möbius convolution factors into W^κ−U^κ and normalization gives the power mean on [U,W] of order κ−1, with the geometric and maximum endpoints. The primewise log is bounded by (2/p) times the indicator of positive valuation, so the expected sup-norm tails on both the integer and geometric-valuation sides are at most 2Σ_{p>P}p⁻². CRT and bounded-Lipschitz approximation thus give the claimed path convergence. A positive valuation makes the local path strictly increasing; almost surely there are infinitely many such valuations. Arbitrarily small prime increments with divergent sum give dense finite subset sums; fixing finitely many valuations and controlling the independent nonnegative tail proves full support. Bernoulli thinning yields an unbounded-in-probability number of fair coin choices; positivity makes each level set an antichain, and convolution cannot increase the maximum atom. Uniform integrability follows by bounding all higher positive moments via the squarefree-divisor product. At κ=2 the a≥1 factor is U+p⁻ᵃ/2; a=0 contributes separately as 1. Summing with the geometric law gives exactly 1+1/[2p(p−1)]. An independent bounded calculation gave 1.4276564870 through p≤10⁶ with omitted log-tail at most 1/(2·10⁶), consistent with the decimal.
residual_risks: The finite arithmetic check does not verify the analytical conclusions. No absolute continuity or convergence rate is asserted.

evidence: Davenport-type results cover the scalar divisor-ratio endpoint; the LCM-sum literature supplies Möbius inversion, the normalization and monotonicity. The directly matching Resultary theorem also covers complex Mellin moments.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Scalar additive-function distribution theory by itself need not imply a parameter-uniform path law. Here the prior proof for the same normalization supplies the requisite uniform estimates, not just a scalar general theorem.

evidence: The prior infinite-products/finite-integer proof gives independent geometric valuations and joint finite-prime convergence, and bounds each nonzero local log by −log(1−1/p), independent of κ and a. It gives an empirical tail bound with weights log(1−1/p)⁻¹/p. Its support and Sperner atomlessness arguments also apply to the identical marginals.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Each finite-prime sum is a continuous path with both endpoints, and joint valuation convergence implies its law converges in C([0,1]). Put the supremum inside the nonnegative sum and dominate each term by the same primewise bound. Expected tails vanish on both sides, giving the full path convergence by the existing truncation method. The same uniform summability makes the prior coupling simultaneously continuous and strictly increasing using any active prime.

originality.rationale: The distinct Resultary finding 2026/10/18/…244008dbe1cb treats the identical normalization, endpoints, marginal support and non-atomicity, common valuation coupling and exact κ=2 mean, and gives the stronger complex Mellin formula. It does not literally state empirical weak convergence in C([0,1]). Its proof nevertheless gives all inputs to that statement: both primewise bounds uniform in κ and joint CRT convergence for each finite set of primes. The same truncation argument therefore proves the joint path-space result directly by applying bounded-Lipschitz tests on C([0,1]) instead of on the scalar logarithms. This is a statement-level and proof-level overlap, not a priority inference from dates.
